subject: tech
title: Keys and Letters
about: Finding his way around a real keyboard: the space bar, enter, backspace, shift and caps lock, the arrow keys, why the letters are not in ABC order (the top row starts Q W E), where the numbers sit, capital letters on the keys but small letters on the screen, where thumbs and pointer fingers rest, and typing his name one key at a time. NC K2-CS-03 (operate software to perform tasks) and K2-CS-02 (hardware parts and what they do). Read it together at a keyboard so he can press each key as it comes up.
tip: Sit him at a real keyboard and let him type his name one key at a time, with shift for the first letter.

cards.q: Which key is the long one at the bottom of the keyboard?
cards.note: The space bar is the longest key. Press it with your thumb to leave a space between words.

cards.q: What does the space bar put between two words?
cards.note: cat dog needs a space in the middle. Without it you get catdog.

cards.q: Which key starts a new line of writing?
cards.note: Enter is also called return. On many keyboards it has a bent arrow on it.

cards.q: You typed the wrong letter. Which key erases the letter before the blinking line?
cards.note: Backspace erases backwards, one letter each press. On some keyboards it is called delete.

cards.q: You want a capital B. What do you hold down while you press B?
cards.note: Hold shift with one hand and tap the letter with the other. Let go and the letters are small again.

cards.q: What do the four arrow keys do?
cards.note: Up, down, left, right. The arrows move your blinking line, the cursor, without erasing anything.

cards.q: Which three letters start the top letter row on a keyboard?
cards.note: Keyboard letters are not in ABC order. Look for the Q at the top left to find your way.

cards.q: Are the letters on a keyboard in ABC order or mixed up?
cards.note: The letters sit in a special order called QWERTY, named for the first six keys in the top row.

cards.q: Where are the number keys on a keyboard?
cards.note: The numbers run in a row above the letters. Some big keyboards have a number pad on the right too.

cards.q: The keys show capital letters. What kind of letters show up on the screen when you type?
cards.note: Keys show capitals so they are easy to read. You get small letters unless you hold shift.

cards.q: Which fingers rest on the space bar?
cards.note: Thumbs tap the space bar. The other fingers reach for the letters.

cards.q: On the F and J keys you can feel tiny bumps. Which fingers go there?
cards.note: Feel the bumps on F and J. Your pointer fingers rest there so your hands know where they are.

cards.q: You want to type your name. How do you do it?
cards.note: Find each letter and press it once. Hold shift for the capital letter at the start.

cards.q: You want a whole word in CAPITAL letters. What locks the capitals on?
cards.sayQ: You want a whole word in capital letters. What locks the capitals on?
cards.note: Caps lock keeps every letter capital until you press it again. A little light may show it is on.

cards.q: You hold a key down too long and get aaaaa. How many times should you press a key for one letter?
cards.sayQ: You hold a key down too long and the same letter comes out again and again. How many times should you press a key for one letter?
cards.note: Press and let go. Holding a key down makes the letter repeat and repeat.

cards.q: Which hands do good typists use?
cards.note: Left hand on the left side, right hand on the right. Each hand takes care of its own keys.

cards.q: You typed a word in the search box. Which key tells the computer go?
cards.note: Enter means go. It sends your words off, or starts a new line when you are writing.
